title: Toolcall Translation Service and Telemetry Backfill
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Add a lightweight Translation Proxy service that reconciles OpenAI-style tool descriptors and legacy function-based invocation metadata at runtime, plus a telemetry backfill pipeline to seed mappings and measure resolution accuracy. The goal is a low-latency shim that minimizes integration friction for customers migrating between tool/function surfaces while preserving strong observability and opt-out controls for Private deployments.
background: Customers and internal integrations are increasingly hitting mismatches between OpenAI-style tool metadata (name/description/parameters) and our legacy function ecosystem. Current in-runtime heuristics are ad-hoc, brittle, and hard to audit. We need a deterministic, observable service that centralizes mapping decisions, supports staged rollouts, and allows automated backfilling of historical calls into the canonical registry.
goals: Provide deterministic name/parameter mapping for >95% of production tool calls with sub-15ms median added latency
Expose mapping decisions and confidence via telemetry for Console and monitoring
Support multiple resolution strategies (alias table, tokenized fuzzy match, optional ML reranker) with feature flags per deployment type
Backfill historical legacy function invocations into canonical registry to seed mappings and improve matching coverage
Ensure Private/VPC customers can opt out of telemetry and ML-based matching (local-only rules)
success_metrics: Mapping coverage >= 95% for top 200 tool names (per-customer) after backfill
False-positive mapping rate <= 1% on canary traffic
Median added p99 latency from proxy < 30ms (goal: < 15ms)
Telemetry-backed precision/recall dashboard available in Console (per-customer and global)
No customer-facing errors introduced during canary rollout
design_notes: Architecture: Lightweight stateless translation proxy colocated at the edge of the runtime routing layer. Resolution pipeline: 1) exact alias registry lookup (primary), 2) normalized token match (stemming/punctuation rules) with edit-distance thresholds, 3) optional reranker that uses lightweight signal features (historical invocation counts, description similarity) and returns confidence score. Cache results per model/route with TTL and invalidation hooks on registry updates. Telemetry emitted as anonymized resolution events with confidence and chosen strategy. For Private customers, the proxy can be configured to run in 'local-only' mode with telemetry disabled. Avoid putting heavy ML models inline; ML reranker should be a microservice with separate scaling and opt-in.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Alias registry schema and management API (read/write, audit log). Implement simple alias import from CSV and admin UI hooks.
Phase 2: Translation Proxy runtime implementation (Go) with exact and tokenized matchers, in-memory LRU cache, TTL, and metrics (Prometheus).
Phase 3: Telemetry backfill pipeline (Spark/Beam job) that consumes historical invocation logs, computes candidate mappings, and writes suggested aliases to a staging table for curator review.
Phase 4: Optional ML reranker service (Python) trained on curated pairs from backfill. Expose as HTTP endpoint with request batching and strict latency budgets.
Phase 5: Console integration: mapping dashboard, suggestion review UX, and per-customer opt-outs.
Phase 6: Canary rollout with progressive traffic ramp and monitoring alarms. Followed by full rollout and deprecation plan for old heuristics.
rollout_plan: Start with internal runtime-only canary (10% of internal services) for 2 weeks
Open canary to a subset of low-risk customers (opt-in) with mailbox and Slack channel for feedback
Enable telemetry backfill in parallel but do not auto-apply suggested aliases until curator approval
Ramp to 50% production traffic if false-positive rate < 0.5% over 24h, else iterate
Full enablement with feature flags and a 2-week observability hold, then schedule deprecation of legacy heuristics
testing: Unit tests for registry CRUD and resolution strategies
Integration tests that simulate mixed tool/function traffic and assert correct mapping decisions
Performance tests to verify added latency at median and p99 under representative QPS
A/B test harness for canary customers to measure user-visible regressions
Privacy tests to ensure telemetry payloads contain no PII and respect Private opt-outs
risks_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect mapping could trigger wrong tool execution. Mitigation: Fail closed to legacy behavior when confidence < threshold and emit alerts.
Risk: Latency regression. Mitigation: Keep exact-alias path in hot path; run ML reranker asynchronously with best-effort fallback.
Risk: Telemetry concerns for Private customers. Mitigation: Add opt-out and local-only mode; encrypt telemetry in transit and store only aggregate metrics for hosted customers.
Risk: Curator bandwidth to review backfill suggestions. Mitigation: Prioritize suggestions by invocation volume and automatic acceptance rules for high-confidence matches.
dependencies: ENG-29500 (runtime routing hooks for proxy placement)
PM-412 (console mapping UX and review workflow)
SEC-88 (telemetry data retention and PII review)
